arxiv-1804-09188.title: Work Statistics, Loschmidt Echo and Information Scrambling in Chaotic Quantum Systems
arxiv-1804-09188.creator: Aurélia Chenu, Javier Molina-Vilaplana, Adolfo del Campo
arxiv-1804-09188.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Aurélia Chenu, Javier Molina-Vilaplana, Adolfo del Campo. Characterizing the work statistics of driven complex quantum systems is generally challenging because of the exponential growth with the system size of the number of transitions involved between different energy levels. We consider the quantum work distribution associated with the driving of chaotic quantum systems described by random matrix Hamiltonians and characterize exactly the work statistics associated with a sudden quench for arbitrary temperature and system size.

arxiv-1908-02870.title: Population collapse in Elite-dominated societies: A differential equations model without differential equations
arxiv-1908-02870.description: Abstract . The HANDY model of Motesharrei, Rivas, and Kalnay examines interactions with the environment by human populations, both between poor and rich people, i.e. , “Commoners” and “Elites”. The Elites control the society’s wealth and consume it at a higher rate than Commoners, whose work produces the wealth.

arxiv-2109-14819.title: Quantum Information Masking of Hadamard Sets
arxiv-2109-14819.creator: Bao-Zhi Sun, Shao-Ming Fei, Xianqing Li-Jost
arxiv-2109-14819.description: Abstract We study quantum information masking of arbitrary dimensional states. Given a set of fixed reducing pure states, we study the linear combinations of them, such that they all have the same marginal states with the given ones. We define the so called Hadamard set of quantum states whose Gram-Schmidt matrix can be diagonalized by Hadamard unitary matrices.

arxiv-2112-09457.title: Quantum Computer Benchmarking via Quantum Algorithms
arxiv-2112-09457.creator: Konstantinos Georgopoulos, Clive Emary, Paolo Zuliani
arxiv-2112-09457.description: Abstract We present a framework that utilizes quantum algorithms, an architecture aware quantum noise model and an ideal simulator to benchmark quantum computers. The benchmark metrics highlight the difference between the quantum computer evolution and the simulated noisy and ideal quantum evolutions. We utilize our framework for benchmarking three IBMQ systems.

arxiv-2211-10118.title: Exploring the Phase Diagram of V-QCD with Neutron Star Merger Simulations
arxiv-2211-10118.creator: \firstname Tuna \lastname Demircik, \firstname Christian \lastname Ecker \fnsep, \firstname Matti \lastname Järvinen, \firstname Luciano \lastname Rezzolla, \firstname Samuel \lastname Tootle, \firstname Konrad \lastname Topolski
arxiv-2211-10118.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by \firstname Tuna \lastname Demircik, \firstname Christian \lastname Ecker \fnsep, \firstname Matti \lastname Järvinen, \firstname Luciano \lastname Rezzolla, \firstname Samuel \lastname Tootle, \firstname Konrad \lastname Topolski. Determining the phase structure of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and its Equation of State (EOS) at densities and temperatures realized inside neutron stars and their mergers is a long-standing open problem.

arxiv-2308-06688.title: DETERMINING A STATIONARY MEAN FIELD GAME SYSTEM FROM FULL/PARTIAL BOUNDARY MEASUREMENT
arxiv-2308-06688.creator: Ming-Hui Ding, Hongyu Liu, Guang-Hui Zheng
arxiv-2308-06688.description: Abstract ABSTRACT In this paper, we propose and study the utilization of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann (DN) map to uniquely identify the discount functions r,k and cost function F in a stationary mean field game (MFG) system. This study features several technical novelties that make it highly intriguing and challenging. Firstly, it involves a coupling of two nonlinear elliptic partial differential equations.

arxiv-2310-11311.title: Elucidating The Design Space of Classifier-Guided Diffusion Generation
arxiv-2310-11311.creator: Jiajun Ma, Tianyang Hu, Wenjia Wang, Jiacheng Sun
arxiv-2310-11311.description: Abstract Guidance in conditional diffusion generation is of great importance for sample quality and controllability. However, existing guidance schemes are to be desired. On one hand, mainstream methods such as classifier guidance and classifier-free guidance both require extra training with labeled data, which is time-consuming and unable to adapt to new conditions.

arxiv-2405-08705.title: Pfaff’s Method Revisited
arxiv-2405-08705.creator: Aritram Dhar
arxiv-2405-08705.description: Abstract . In 1797, Pfaff gave a simple proof of a F 2 3 {}_{3}F_{2} hypergeometric series summation formula which was much later reproved by Andrews in 1996. In the same paper, Andrews also proved other well-known hypergeometric identities using Pfaff’s method.

arxiv-2409-08006.title: Towards regulatory compliant lifecycle for AI-based medical devices in EU: Industry perspectives Journal: Publication Name
arxiv-2409-08006.creator: Tuomas Granlund, Vlad Stirbu, Tommi Mikkonen
arxiv-2409-08006.description: Abstract Despite the immense potential of AI-powered medical devices to revolutionize healthcare, concerns regarding their safety in life-critical applications remain. While the European regulatory framework provides a comprehensive approach to medical device software development, it falls short in addressing AI-specific considerations.

arxiv-2410-12906.title: Wreathing, Discrete Gauging, and Non-invertible Symmetries
arxiv-2410-12906.creator: Julius F. Grimminger, William Harding, and Noppadol Mekareeya
arxiv-2410-12906.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Julius F. Grimminger, William Harding, and Noppadol Mekareeya. ’t Hooft anomalies of discrete global symmetries and gaugings thereof have rich mathematical structures and far-reaching physical consequences. We examine each subgroup G G , up to automorphisms, of the permutation group S 4 S_{4} that acts on the four legs of the affine D 4 D_{4} quiver diagram, which is mirror dual to the 3d 𝒩 = 4 \mathcal{N}=4 SU ⁡ ( 2 ) \mathrm{SU}(2) gauge theory with four flavours.

arxiv-2504-07898.title: How do Large Language Models Understand Relevance? A Mechanistic Interpretability Perspective CCS: Information systems Language models
arxiv-2504-07898.creator: Qi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Ji-Rong Wen
arxiv-2504-07898.description: Abstract . Recent studies have shown that large language models (LLMs) can assess relevance and support information retrieval (IR) tasks such as document ranking and relevance judgment generation. However, the internal mechanisms by which off-the-shelf LLMs understand and operationalize relevance remain largely unexplored.

arxiv-2601-17909.title: From Statistical Disclosure Control to Fair AI: Navigating Fundamental Tradeoffs in Differential Privacy
arxiv-2601-17909.creator: Adriana Watson
arxiv-2601-17909.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Adriana Watson. Differential privacy has become the gold standard for privacy-preserving machine learning systems. Unfortunately, subsequent work has primarily fixated on the privacy-utility tradeoff, leaving the subject of fairness constraints undervalued and under-researched. This paper provides a systematic treatment connecting three threads: (1) Dalenius’s impossibility results for semantic privacy, (2) Dwork’s differential privacy as an achievable alternative, and (3) emerging impossibility results from the addition of a fairness requirement.

britannica-1911-rich-claudius-james.title: Rich, Claudius James (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rich-claudius-james.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rich-claudius-james.description: Article 'Rich, Claudius James' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 23), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. and scholar, was born near Dijon on the 28th of March 1787. His youth was spent at Bristol. He early developed a gift for languages, becoming familiar not only with Latin and Greek but also with Hebrew, Syriac, Persian, Turkish and other Eastern tongues. In 1804 Rich went to Constantinople, where, and at Smyrna, he stayed some time, perfecting himself in Turkish.

pmc-10648759.title: Yellow Field Pea Protein (Pisum sativum L.): Extraction Technologies, Functionalities, and Applications
pmc-10648759.creator: Nancy D. Asen, Rotimi E. Aluko, Alex Martynenko, Alphonsus Utioh, Pankaj Bhowmik
pmc-10648759.description: Yellow field peas (Pisum sativum L.) hold significant value for producers, researchers, and ingredient manufacturers due to their wealthy composition of protein, starch, and micronutrients. The protein quality in peas is influenced by both intrinsic factors like amino acid composition and spatial conformations and extrinsic factors including growth and processing conditions.

pmc-12431218.title: Brief mindfulness coaching enhances selective attention in medical scientists: A pilot study
pmc-12431218.creator: Satish Jaiswal, Jason Nan, Suzanna R. Purpura, James K. Manchanda, Iris Garcia-pak, Dhakshin S. Ramanathan, Dawna Chuss, Deborah T. Rana, Ellen Beck, Paul A. Insel, Neil C. Chi, David M. Roth, Hemal H. Patel, Jyoti Mishra, Michael B. Steinborn, Michael B. Steinborn, Michael B. Steinborn
pmc-12431218.description: Medical scientists have dual commitments to clinical care and research efforts. Such commitments can create hectic and stressful work schedules, which may impact on well-being and cognition. In this study, we tested the hypothesis that brief mindfulness coaching (three 1.5 hour online group sessions over 12 weeks) can benefit medical scientists.

pmc-12700923.title: Delayed start of estetrol drospirenone versus ethinyl estradiol gestodene for ovulation inhibition in a noninferiority randomized controlled trial
pmc-12700923.creator: Sirarat Ittipuripat, Phanupong Phutrakool, Sutira Uaamnuichai, Gade Porntawansak, Rachanee Wongwathanavikrom, Punyawee Utaipatanacheep, Somsook Santibenchakul
pmc-12700923.description: Delayed-start contraception may reduce the risk of unintended pregnancy; however, data on newer formulations, such as estetrol (E4)-containing pills are limited. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of delayed start combined oral contraceptives (COCs) containing 15 mg E4 and 3 mg drospirenone (E4/DRSP).

pmc-13066646.title: Clay-organic matter interactions drive microbial necromass preservation in soils
pmc-13066646.creator: Xu Wang, Cynthia M Kallenbach, Maya Almaraz, Katerina Georgiou, Lifei Sun, Changpeng Sang, Ping Jiang, Yue Liu, Edith Bai, Chao Wang
pmc-13066646.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microbial necromass is increasingly recognized as a major source of stable soil organic matter (SOM), and its persistence is often attributed to interactions with clay-sized minerals. However, the mechanisms underlying this mineral-mediated stabilization remain poorly understood. Here, we conducted an in situ dual-labeled (13C and 15N) microbial necromass experiment across a clay gradient to quantify how clay content and necromass origin (bacterial vs. fungal) regulate necromass persistence.

pmc-13299981.title: Five-year trends in ablation workflows and outcomes: insights from the EP Device Registry
pmc-13299981.creator: I Deisenhofer, H Ramanna, P Morina Vazquez, O Alcalde Rodriguez, A Roux, R Folkeringa, Z Starek, T Chalvidan, E Komosa, E Zhai, D Steven
pmc-13299981.description: BackgroundAblation workflows are frequently changing as new technologies and techniques are adopted. Here we examine trends in standard-of-care ablation workflows and outcomes across Europe and India since 2020.MethodsTrends were analyzed across primary indications for treatment of AF, SVT, and ventricular arrhythmia (VA) from 3005 subjects enrolled in the EP Device Registry from 2020 to 2024.

pmc-13335427.title: A Chirality‐Converted Bacteriolytic Dodecapeptide Regulates Vibrio‐Induced Polymicrobial Infection and Ameliorates Invasion‐Associated Gut Microbiota Disequilibrium
pmc-13335427.creator: Ping Zeng, Qipeng Cheng, Xiaoxu Zhang, Honglan Wang, Jinghan Zhang, Xinyi Ding, Pengfei Zhang, Lanhua Yi, Kwok‐Yin Wong, Kin‐Fai Chan, Sheng Chen, Sharon Shui Yee Leung
pmc-13335427.description: The polymicrobial infections caused by Vibrio species, especially multidrug‐resistant isolates, are posing increasing threats to the health of coastal residents. Herein, a novel dodecapeptide, denoted as D‐zp37, was designed and synthesized, aiming to combat these notorious pathogens. Experimental results proved that the simple chirality conversion of the parent peptide, zp37, could significantly boost the antibacterial activity and proteolytic stability.

pmc-13408310.title: Development and Characterization of Kombucha Tea Nanoemulsion for Stability, Bioactive Delivery, and Functional Food Applications
pmc-13408310.creator: Thida Kaewkod, Nitsanat Cheepchirasuk, Wipawadee Teppabut, Chayangkorn Kuntolbut, Yingmanee Tragoolpua
pmc-13408310.description: Kombucha is a fermented tea beverage and a rich source of bioactive compounds with potential health benefits. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of different tea substrates (green, oolong, and black tea) on fermentation characteristics, bioactive compound profiles, antioxidant activity, and cytotoxicity, and to develop a nanoemulsion system for the encapsulation of kombucha-derived bioactive compounds for food applications.

pmc-13680507.title: Effective stimulation sites and networks for substantia nigra pars reticulata deep brain stimulation for auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia
pmc-13680507.creator: Min Jae Kim, Ankur Butala, Yousef Salimpour, Akira Sawa, Martijn Figee, Ki Sueng Choi, Anruo Shen, David Schretlen, Kelly A. Mills, Nicola Cascella
pmc-13680507.description: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the substantia nigra pars reticulata (SNpr) is under investigation for managing auditory-verbal hallucinations (AVH) in treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TR-SZ). We assessed acute AVH suppression during initial SNpr-DBS programming in three TR-SZ patients and mapped associated brain network engagement using normative connectomes.

uslaw-usc-t28-s2255.title: 28 U.S.C. § 2255 — Federal custody; remedies on motion attacking sentence
uslaw-usc-t28-s2255.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s2255.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part VI (Particular Proceedings); Chapter 153 (Habeas Corpus). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) A prisoner in custody under sentence of a court established by Act of Congress claiming the right to be released upon the ground that the sentence was imposed in violation of the Constitution or laws of the United States.

uslaw-usc-t36-s20304.title: 36 U.S.C. § 20304 — Powers
uslaw-usc-t36-s20304.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t36-s20304.description: United States Code, Title 36 (Patriotic And National Observances, Ceremonies, And Organizations); Part B (Organizations); Chapter 203 (American Academy Of Arts And Letters). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The corporation may— (1) adopt bylaws and regulations; (2) fill vacancies; (3) provide for the election of foreign, domestic, or honorary associate members, and the division of those members into classes; (4) receive bequests.
